# Was Rackspace Spot hacked?

**Reported.** Reportedly yes: Rackspace's customer notice, as BleepingComputer quotes it, says leaked credentials let an unauthorized party into Spot on Nov 17. No Rackspace page carries it. Data theft, customer count and attacker are not established.

Incident: Rackspace Spot breach, Nov 2026. Also reported as the Rackspace Spot outage and the Rackspace Spot Kubernetes breach. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 6:09 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Rackspace, Platform9, BleepingComputer, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 6:09 PM ET: **Rackspace reportedly told customers leaked credentials let someone into Spot on Nov 17; not confirmed on a Rackspace page.** First draft. 3 sources (2 Tier 1, 1 Tier 2), 11 claims (2 Confirmed, 5 Reported, 4 Not established), 5 questions. BleepingComputer, Nov 21, quotes Rackspace's customer notice: unauthorized access with leaked credentials, pods created, Kubernetes Secrets readable, admin console down for days, service restored Nov 21. Rackspace's own release notes and status page (Tier 1) do not mention a breach, so the hack stays Reported. Data theft, number of customers, attacker and how the credentials leaked are Not established. BleepingComputer was read through a fetch tool because the site blocks direct automated reading. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. Rackspace Spot runs customers' Kubernetes clusters, and the admin console was down for days. Rackspace reportedly says some customer organizations were affected. The number is unknown.
- Who is affected: Organizations that run workloads on Rackspace Spot. Rackspace reportedly told affected customers to reissue Spot API tokens, replace refresh tokens, download new kubeconfig files and rotate credentials in cluster Secrets. Other customers should watch Rackspace's notices.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 17 | Reported access window (UTC) | About 00:20 to 22:00 UTC, per the notice |
| Nov 21 | Service reportedly restored | Per BleepingComputer; console was down for days |
| Nov 25 | New sign-ups restricted until | 17:00 UTC, on Rackspace's status page |

### Known so far

- Rackspace's release notes list a November 2026 fix that closed a network exposure on Spot worker nodes as part of security hardening.
- Rackspace's Spot status page says new sign-ups are restricted until Nov 25, 17:00 UTC after recent system maintenance.

### Not known yet

- Whether Rackspace itself has confirmed the breach on a page it hosts. Reports rely on a customer notice.
- Whether customer data or Secrets were actually read or misused, not just readable.
- How many customers were affected.
- How the credentials leaked, whose they were, and who used them.
- Whether the full restoration Nov 21 is confirmed by Rackspace on its own pages.
